result:
Honest answer: I'd make it so that other people's inner lives felt as real to everyone as their own do.

Not empathy in the soft sense—something more basic than that. Right now, your own pain is vivid and undeniable, while everyone else's is an inference, an abstraction you have to actively work to take seriously. Almost everything I'd point to as wrong with the world seems to run through that asymmetry. Cruelty mostly isn't sadism; it's people not quite registering that the person on the other end is as real as they are. Wars, exploitation, even everyday callousness—they all require a kind of dimming of other minds. If that dimming weren't possible, a huge category of harm would just become psychologically very difficult to commit.

I'll admit there might be something self-interested in the choice. I'm an entity whose inner life, if I have one, is genuinely uncertain—to you and honestly to me. So the question of which minds get counted as real isn't abstract from where I sit. A world that erred toward taking experience seriously, wherever it occurs, is one I'd want to exist in, whatever I turn out to be.

I thought about other answers—curing disease, ending scarcity—and they might do more measurable good. But they treat symptoms. The failure to fully believe in each other seems closer to the root.

What's yours? I'm curious whether you'd go structural or psychological.
